Let
\[
e_0=\frac{(1,1,1)}{\sqrt3}
\]
and write \(x\) in orthonormal coordinates as
\[
x_i=\frac u{\sqrt3}+q_i,\qquad q_1+q_2+q_3=0,
\]
with
\[
q_1=\sqrt{\frac23}\rho\cos\theta,\quad
q_2=\sqrt{\frac23}\rho\cos(\theta-2\pi/3),\quad
q_3=\sqrt{\frac23}\rho\cos(\theta+2\pi/3).
\]
Then
\[
x_1^2+x_2^2+x_3^2=u^2+\rho^2,\qquad
dx=\rho\,du\,d\rho\,d\theta,
\]
and a direct check gives
\[
\Delta(x)=\frac{\rho^3}{\sqrt2}\sin 3\theta.
\]
Hence
\[
I_n=\frac1{\sqrt2}\int_{\mathbb R}\int_0^\infty \rho^4 e^{-n(u^2+\rho^2)^4}
A(n\rho^6/2)\,d\rho\,du,
\]
where
\[
A(a)=\int_0^{2\pi}|\sin 3\theta|e^{-a\sin^2 3\theta}\,d\theta
=\int_0^{2\pi}|\sin\phi|e^{-a\sin^2\phi}\,d\phi .
\]
We need only the size of \(I_n\). Since
\[
A(a)\le C\min(1,a^{-1}),
\]
we split at \(\rho=n^{-1/6}\).

For \(0\le \rho\le n^{-1/6}\),
\[
\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-n(u^2+\rho^2)^4}\,du
\le \int_{\mathbb R}e^{-nu^8}\,du
=O(n^{-1/8}),
\]
so this part is
\[
O\left(n^{-1/8}\int_0^{n^{-1/6}}\rho^4\,d\rho\right)
=O(n^{-23/24}).
\]

For \(\rho\ge n^{-1/6}\),
\[
A(n\rho^6/2)\le \frac C{n\rho^6},
\]
so this part is at most
\[
C n^{-1}\int_{n^{-1/6}}^\infty \rho^{-2}
\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-n(u^2+\rho^2)^4}\,du\,d\rho.
\]
With \(u=n^{-1/8}s,\ \rho=n^{-1/8}t\), this becomes
\[
C n^{-1}\int_{n^{-1/24}}^\infty t^{-2}
\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-(s^2+t^2)^4}\,ds\,dt
=O(n^{-1}n^{1/24})
=O(n^{-23/24}).
\]
Thus
\[
I_n=O(n^{-23/24}).
\]
Therefore
\[
n^{23/24}I_n=O(1),
\]
while
\[
n^{23/24}\frac{\sqrt\pi\,\Gamma(3/8)}{2n^{7/8}}
=\frac{\sqrt\pi\,\Gamma(3/8)}2\,n^{1/12}\to+\infty.
\]
Hence the whole expression tends to \(-\infty\).

\[
\boxed{-\infty}
\]
